Seminar Title:

Integrated Flow and Sediment Transport Modelling of Mahanadi River

Seminar Type:

Contact:

Anurag Sharma

Abstract:

Sediment transport is a complex and highly variable process that influences river morphology, channel stability, hydraulic infrastructure, coastal stability and aquatic ecosystems. Accurate assessment of sediment transport is a challenging task due of its nonlinear nature under different flow and channel conditions. In large alluvial rivers such as the Mahanadi, variations in flow conditions, sediment characteristics, and channel geometry, make sediment transport difficult to assess using a single approach. Therefore, this study focuses on investigating the flow and sediment transport characteristics of the Mahanadi River using data-driven, numerical, experimental, and entropy-based approaches. Historical hydrological and sediment data will be used for sediment discharge and suspended sediment concentration prediction using Sediment Rating Curves (SRC), Machine Learning (ML), and Deep Learning (DL) techniques, along with Explainable AI (XAI) to analyse the influence of input variables. Flow and sediment transport processes will further be investigated using HEC-RAS and MIKE 21 FM to examine the hydraulic and sediment movement of the selected river reach under different flow conditions. Flume experimentation will be conducted in a mobile-bed channel under flow and channel conditions representative of the Mahanadi River, to examine flow characteristics and sediment transport. In addition, an entropy-based approach will be applied to estimate cross-sectional discharge and assess bed-load transport using the reconstructed velocity field. The study will integrate these approaches to obtain a comprehensive understanding of flow and sediment transport dynamics in the Mahanadi River and provide a better understanding and management of sediment transport in large alluvial rivers.
